response.title: What's the simplest way to have air conditioning in a truck bed camper for a weekend with no hookups: battery AC, power station, or generator?
response.answer:
For a truck bed camper with no hookups for an entire weekend, I'd recommend a small inverter generator + a compact air conditioner if you want reliable cooling without spending thousands on batteries.

If you prioritize quiet operation, a portable power station is more convenient, but keeping an AC running for two nights takes considerably more battery capacity than most people expect.

Comparing your three options

Option

	

Simplicity

Generator + AC

Power station + AC

Good with a large enough battery

Battery-powered AC

	

Compact, integrated

	

Usually limited without extra batteries

	

Short runtime, high cost

The important distinction is that a battery-powered AC has its own battery, while a power station lets you power a separate AC unit. Both ultimately face the same energy limitations.

How much battery do you actually need?

Assume a small 5,000 BTU air conditioner consuming 500 watts while running.

Assumes continuous compressor operation, 85% usable AC output efficiency, and no recharging. Actual cycling may reduce consumption.

For two eight-hour nights, even a modest 500W AC could require around 9.4 kWh of battery capacity. That's a lot to carry in a pickup camper.

What I'd actually set up
Shop

Option A: Generator + small AC

Choose a roughly 2,000W-class inverter generator and a 5,000 BTU window AC, provided the generator can handle its starting surge. This is the most practical setup for long cooling sessions.

Shop

Option B: Integrated battery AC

A camping-specific unit such as the EcoFlow WAVE 3 is easier to set up and doesn't require a separate generator. But plan for additional batteries or charging if you need cooling across multiple nights.

One important safety consideration: never operate a generator in the truck bed under a camper, inside the camper, or near its openings. Keep it outdoors at least 20 feet away from occupied structures and air intakes, direct exhaust away, and use a working CO alarm. 
U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission
+1
 Generator restrictions and quiet hours may also rule out overnight operation.

I need AC running all night while sleeping
Just 2–4 hours before bedtime
Mostly during hot afternoons
Find my best setup

This determines whether a relatively small battery system is realistic or whether a generator is worth the extra hassle.

| Option | Simplicity | Weekend cooling | Main downside |
|---|---|---|---|

## How much battery do you actually need?

Assume a small 5,000 BTU air conditioner consuming 500 watts while running.

{@body const [hours,setHours] = DIL.useState(8)}
{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState("500")}
{@body const [nights,setNights] = DIL.useState("2")}
{@body const energy = Number(watts)*hours*Number(nights)/0.85/1000}

  <text weight="medium">Weekend battery calculator</text>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">AC running power</text>
    <segmented-control size="md" value={watts} onChange={setWatts} options={[{label:"300W",value:"300"},{label:"500W",value:"500"},{label:"700W",value:"700"}]}/>
  </row>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Nights</text>
    <segmented-control size="md" value={nights} onChange={setNights} options={[{label:"1",value:"1"},{label:"2",value:"2"},{label:"3",value:"3"}]}/>
  </row>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">Hours of AC per night</text>
    **{hours} hours**
  </row>
  <slider min={2} max={12} step={1} value={hours} onChange={setHours}/>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="lg" padding={3} gap={1}>
    <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">Estimated battery capacity needed</text>
    <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{energy.toFixed(1)} kWh</title>
    <text size="xs" color="secondary">Assumes continuous compressor operation, 85% usable AC output efficiency, and no recharging. Actual cycling may reduce consumption.</text>
  </box>
</box>

For two eight-hour nights, even a modest 500W AC could require around 9.4 kWh of battery capacity. That's a lot to carry in a pickup camper.

    Choose a roughly 2,000W-class inverter generator and a 5,000 BTU window AC, provided the generator can handle its starting surge. This is the most practical setup for long cooling sessions.

One important safety consideration: **never operate a generator in the truck bed under a camper, inside the camper, or near its openings.** Keep it outdoors at least 20 feet away from occupied structures and air intakes, direct exhaust away, and use a working CO alarm. <Cite refs={["turn409185search13","turn409185search7"]}/> Generator restrictions and quiet hours may also rule out overnight operation.
